Confusable pairs among the stopping rules, distances and conduct rules in this section, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in trailing lines.

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A03
A two-lane road with a center turning lane and a four-lane road with no median both require traffic in both directions to stop for a school bus, while a divided highway with a median or a road of four or more lanes with a turning lane requires only following traffic to stop. [A03]
Why it matters: group school bus; difficulty high; confusable road layouts.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A02
The school bus stop applies whenever the stop arm is out or the red lights flash, and it lasts until the arm is withdrawn, the lights go off and the bus moves again, not just until the children have crossed. [A02]
Why it matters: group school bus; misconception target.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A03
The parking buffer near an emergency vehicle stopped at a crash is 100 feet, while the buffer from fire trucks answering an alarm is one block. [A03]
Why it matters: group emergency distances; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A03
Drivers in both directions yield to an approaching emergency vehicle, and the only exception is opposite-direction traffic on a four-lane limited-access highway with a center median. [A03]
Why it matters: group emergency vehicles; confusable with the school bus median rule.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A04
With two or more lanes in your direction the move-over law means changing lanes away from the stopped vehicle, but with only one lane it means slowing to a reduced safe speed. [A04]
Why it matters: group move-over; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A04
When police signal you and no safe stop exists, you slow by about 10 mph with four-way flashers and keep going, rather than stopping in the travel lane. [A04]
Why it matters: group traffic stop; confusable with stopping for an approaching emergency vehicle.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A05
You must identify yourself and produce your license and registration, but after that answering further questions is your choice. [A05]
Why it matters: group traffic stop; confusable duty versus choice.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A01
A pedestrian crossing on green has the right of way even over a turning car, while a pedestrian should not start crossing on red or yellow. [A01]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A02
Walk and Don't Walk signals, when operating, override the regular traffic lights for pedestrians. [A02]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; confusable pedestrian signal versus traffic signal.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A06
Passing farm equipment in a no-passing zone is illegal, and the only advisable pass is after the operator pulls off the road to let traffic by. [A06]
Why it matters: group farm equipment; misconception target.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0053]
